Hi all,

I'm the_federalist and I am the new moderator of /v/comedy! I don't really have all the "rules" worked out yet. Here are some thoughts:

  • This sub is for sharing video and audio links of stand-up comedy, sketch comedy, or improv comedy. Please no links to text or self-posts without a [META] tag--and in those cases, the post ought to be relevant to questions about the sub itself.

  • You should assume that the content in this sub is for audiences who are adults. If you are someone who is sensitive to material that is politically, racially, or religiously insensitive, it is highly likely that you will be offended by something linked here. You may want to consider starting a comedy sub that is specific to a particular audience or type of material if you feel strongly about this.

  • Not everyone is going to agree about what's funny. If you don't think a link is funny, feel free to use the downvote arrow. If you have a critique of the material I encourage you to add that to the discussion in the comments. However, this is a sub for entertainment. People come here to laugh. This is not a place to wage war on those whose politics or sense of humor differs from yours.

  • Comedy is, by its very nature, often offensive to someone. If you are offended by something that someone shared here, you will get no sympathy from me--I will not remove any links unless there is something illegal about the material. Furthermore, in the comments area, the downvote arrow is not an "I disagree" arrow, nor is it an "I don't like your politics" or an "I don't like your sense of humor" arrow.

I was asked in another sub about why I wanted to moderate this space. This was my response:

I want to moderate the space because I love the art of stand-up comedy and because I want to make sure the space is one that promotes and maintains free expression, showcases comedians from all time periods (from vaudeville era to the early days of what we now know as stand-up to contemporary comics), and protects people's ability to share comedy from edgy and controversial comedians as well as safer comedy. However, it's also important to keep the space focused on comedy as an artform and not joke-sharing. There are already subs here devoted to jokes. I would want to make sure that it retains a distinct identity.

That's enough from me. If you have any suggestions or questions please put them in the comments below or send a message to me. Thanks!
